chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

Indeed Allah is One, and He loves oddness; so three handfuls may suffice you for wudu (ablution): one for the face, and two for the two forearms. And you wipe with the moisture of your right hand your forelock, and with what remains of the moisture of your right hand the top of your right foot, and you wipe with the moisture of your left hand the top of your left foot.

key_terms.الذِّرَاعَيْنِ: the two forearms, which are washed in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوَجْهِ: the face, which is washed in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before acts of worship
key_terms.بِلَّةِ: remaining wetness or moisture on the hand used for wiping
key_terms.ظَهْرَ قَدَمِكَ: the top of your foot, the place wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.غُرَفَاتٍ: handfuls of water used in performing wudu (ablution)
key_terms.نَاصِيَتَكَ: your forelock, the front part of the head to be wiped
key_terms.وَتْرٌ: One; odd-numbered, indicating singularity and preference for the odd

ai.seo_question: How many handfuls of water are sufficient for wudu (ablution) according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام explains the sufficiency of a minimal wudu (ablution) using three handfuls of water. It outlines the distribution of water for washing and the method of wiping the head and feet, linking this practice to Allah's love of what is odd-numbered.
